subject: Economics
description: IRDAI, LIC, GIC, sectors, FDI limits, key schemes, recent reforms

questions.stem: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) was established under the:
questions.explanation: IRDA Act 1999 — set up IRDAI in April 2000 to regulate the insurance sector following its opening to private players (Malhotra Committee, 1994). Headquartered in Hyderabad. Renamed IRDAI in 2014. Issues licences, monitors solvency, prescribes rules, settles disputes. Reports to MoF. Currently chaired by Debasish Panda (since 2022). Insurance Act 1938 is the basic insurance legislation; LIC Act 1956 nationalised life insurance (245 private insurers merged into LIC).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: LIC of India was nationalised on:
questions.explanation: LIC Act 1956 — nationalised 245 private life insurers into LIC. Operations began 1 September 1956. Headquartered in Mumbai (Yogakshema Building). LIC IPO — May 2022 — government divested 3.5% stake; 2nd largest IPO ever in India (₹21,000 crore). Currently 32 life insurers in India (1 public + 31 private) and 26 general insurers + 4 specialised + several health insurers. General Insurance Corporation (GIC) — 1972, holds 4 subsidiaries (now separated): NIA, OIC, NIC, UIIC. Disinvested 2023.

questions.stem: FDI cap in insurance sector — most-recently set at:
questions.explanation: FDI history in insurance: 26% (2000, on opening), 49% (2015 Insurance Amendment Act), 74% (Budget 2021, Finance Act 2021). Up to 74% under automatic route, with conditions on Indian-controlled board. Insurance intermediaries (brokers, agents) → 100%. Lloyds India, reinsurance branches allowed. Budget 2024-25 hinted at allowing 100% FDI in insurance, possibly via Ins. Amendment Bill — under consideration.

questions.stem: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) — launched 2015 — provides life insurance cover of:
questions.explanation: PMJJBY — launched 9 May 2015. Life insurance cover ₹2 lakh, available to individuals 18-50 with savings bank account, paid via auto-debit. Annual premium ~₹436 (raised in 2022 from ₹330). Underwritten by LIC (also private insurers). PMSBY (Suraksha Bima Yojana) — accident + disability insurance ₹2 lakh, premium just ₹20/yr (raised from ₹12 in 2022). APY (Atal Pension Yojana) — pension scheme. Together — JANSURAKSHA suite providing financial security to underprivileged.

questions.stem: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — crop-insurance scheme launched 2016 — replaced:

options.option_text: NAIS (National Agricultural Insurance Scheme) and MNAIS

questions.explanation: PMFBY — launched 13 January 2016 (Sehore, MP). Replaced NAIS (1999) and MNAIS (2010). Aims to provide affordable crop insurance for farmers — premium just 1.5% (rabi), 2% (kharif), 5% (commercial) of insured sum; rest subsidised by Centre + State. AY 2020 — voluntary participation (was mandatory for loanee farmers earlier). Implemented by AIC (Agriculture Insurance Company of India) + private insurers. Covers natural calamities, pests, diseases. Around 5-6 crore farmers enrolled annually. PMFBY is the largest crop-insurance program in the world by area covered.

questions.stem: AYUSHMAN BHARAT — Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), launched 2018 — provides annual health cover up to:

options.option_text: ₹5 lakh per family per year (secondary + tertiary care)

questions.explanation: PM-JAY (launched 23 September 2018, Ranchi) — health cover ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary + tertiary care hospitalisation. Beneficiaries identified via SECC 2011 — ~10.74 crore poor + vulnerable families = ~50 crore people. World's largest government-funded health insurance scheme. Cashless + paperless treatment at ~28,000 empanelled hospitals (PMJAY portal). National Health Authority (NHA) implements. Senior citizens (70+) added September 2024 — irrespective of income/SECC eligibility.

questions.stem: Insurance penetration in India (premiums as % of GDP) currently is approximately:
questions.explanation: Insurance Penetration: Premiums / GDP. India's penetration (Swiss Re Sigma 2023): Total ~4.0%; Life ~3.0%; Non-life ~1.0%. Global average ~7% (advanced economies typically 8-10%). India ranks ~10th in life insurance worldwide by premium volume. Insurance density (premium per capita) much lower in India ($90) vs US ($8,000). IRDAI's 'Insurance for All by 2047' vision aims to dramatically raise penetration via simpler products, regulatory ease (Bima Sugam, Bima Vahak), and digital onboarding.
